acceptance: take and takeover of an active-batch member by a worker other than the owner are refused with a gate code naming the owner; the owner's take succeeds; members of aborted or completed batches follow ordinary claim rules.

Owner recovery succeeds only with the exact current owner and generation plus a reason, is recorded in batch and member session history, and leaves the previous generation stale; a wrong expected owner or generation is refused.
The batch read tool returns registry, receipts, recorded advances and the final-PR binding, paging any field that exceeds the response cap.
todo-db tests cover each behaviour; the foreign-take test fails against 0.12.0 behaviour.
context: Decision gate: start only after todo-db-batch-v2-contract-20261101 is done; implement the merged ADR, and amend the ADR first if implementation shows it is wrong. Guardrails: work in joeharris76/todo-db under its own repository rules, on a branch and PR, never directly on main; never patch the vendored wheel in BenchBox; one server stays one worker identity (todo-db ADRs 0003 and 0006); every new refusal fails closed with a gate code and recovery steps; BenchBox line citations refer to the vendored 0.12.0 wheel (_project/scripts/vendor/todo_db-0.12.0-py3-none-any.whl), so re-read todo-db main before editing; tests prove behaviour, never wiring.
description: Implement the ownership parts of the batch v2 ADR in joeharris76/todo-db. take and takeover of a member of an active batch by anyone but the registered owner are refused. A new session can recover batch ownership after the leader dies by naming the exact current owner and generation and a reason, audited on the batch and its members. A read tool returns the batch registry, receipts, advances and final-PR binding within the 16 KiB response cap. Today an unrelated session can take a registered member, after which the leader's take fails with 'claimed by' (fixture, 2026-11-01); abort and bind need the original owner, so a dead leader strands the batch.
